title: Rabbi David Tawil: Understanding the Amida- "Al Ha'saddikim - Kiddush Hashem"

chapters.about: Amidah, Yom HaShoah, removing evil and adding good

chapters.title: Defining Tzadik and Chasid
chapters.about: Rabbeinu Avraham ben HaRambam, HaMaspik LeOvdei Hashem

chapters.title: The Remnant of Scholars
chapters.about: Peletat Beit Soferhem, religious persecution, martyrs

chapters.title: Conclusion and Legacy
chapters.about: Sacrifice, living in a free country, honoring memory

claims: "The class concludes by discussing the privilege of living in a free country and the importance of sacrificing a little bit of ourselves to honor the memory of those who came before us." - The teacher does mention this, but it is not the conclusion of the class; the class concludes with a final blessing (Baruch Adonai LeOlam, Amen VeAmen) after the discussion on sacrifice.
summary: Rabbi Tawil explains the beracha of Al HaTzadikim in the Amidah, detailing the distinction between the righteous and the pious and the importance of supporting those who uphold Torah values. He connects the themes of this prayer to the memory of those who died al kiddush Hashem throughout history, including the martyrs of the Holocaust. The class concludes by discussing the privilege of living in a free country and the importance of sacrificing a little bit of ourselves to honor the memory of those who came before us.
questions: What is the difference between a Tzadik and a Chasid?
Why does the Amidah pray for the elders?
What does it mean to be a martyr in Judaism?
How does the beracha of Al HaTzadikim relate to the Holocaust?
Why is it important to have our portion with the righteous?
